docs.t: 2d Cir. — Renew your admission every five years, $25
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Renew your admission every five years, $25. You are admitted for five years and must file a renewal application to stay admitted. If you miss it by more than a month you go to inactive status and must renew before you can practice before the court. After 12 months inactive you are removed from the roll and have to reapply from scratch. The renewal fee is $25 (FJC 2024). (2d Cir. LR 46.1)

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000. A principal brief is acceptable at no more than 14,000 words and a reply at no more than 7,000, which is more than FRAP’s 13,000 and 6,500. In cross-appeals the appellant’s principal and response-and-reply briefs get 14,000 each, the appellee’s principal-and-response brief 16,500, and the appellee’s reply 7,000. An amicus brief may be half the length of a party’s principal brief. (LR 32.1(a)(4); LR 28.1.1; LR 29.1)

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Special appendix
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Special appendix. The Second Circuit requires a special appendix with the decision under review and the key statutes and rules. (2d Cir. Local R. 32.1)

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — You ask the clerk for your briefing deadline
docs.x: 2d Cir.. You ask the clerk for your briefing deadline. Within 14 days after the ready date (the later of receiving the last transcript, filing a certificate that none will be ordered, or the record’s filing in a FRAP 15 case) the appellant tells the clerk in writing the deadline it wants, within 91 days of the ready date. If you don’t, the brief is due 40 days after the ready date. The appellee does the same within 14 days after the last appellant’s brief, within 91 days, or defaults to 30 days. In cross-appeals the cap is 60 days. The reply is due 21 days after the last appellee’s brief. The court ordinarily “so orders” the dates you request as firm. (LR 31.2(a))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Extensions are granted only for extraordinary circumstances
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Extensions are granted only for extraordinary circumstances. Absent an extraordinary circumstance, such as serious illness or a death in counsel’s immediate family, the court won’t extend the time to file a brief. The deadline stays in effect unless the court orders otherwise. Disclose any prior motion and its ruling, and move as soon as practicable. (LR 27.1(f))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Ask to file an oversized brief at least 14 days early
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Ask to file an oversized brief at least 14 days early. The court disfavors them. State the length you want and why. An untimely motion is denied absent extraordinary circumstances. (LR 27.1(e))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Six paper copies of every brief and appendix
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Six paper copies of every brief and appendix. A counseled party must submit 6 paper copies of each brief, and 6 of the appendix where one is required. A pro se party submits 3 appendix copies. The six-copy rule is in addition to electronic filing. (LR 31.1; LR 30.1(b))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — File the Acknowledgment and Notice of Appearance within 14 days
docs.x: 2d Cir.. File the Acknowledgment and Notice of Appearance within 14 days. All parties file the court’s Acknowledgment and Notice of Appearance Form within 14 days after the docketing notice. Counsel listed must be admitted here or have an admission application pending. An appellant who doesn’t may be dismissed, and an appellee may be barred from being heard. (LR 12.3)

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Counseled civil appellants file Forms C and D in 14 days
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Counseled civil appellants file Forms C and D in 14 days. Within 14 days after the notice of appeal, a counseled civil appellant files Form C, the Civil Appeal Pre-Argument Statement with its addenda, and Form D, the transcript information form. Failure may result in dismissal. (LR 12.1)

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Oral argument is requested by form, or it’s waived
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Oral argument is requested by form, or it’s waived. Each party must file an Oral Argument Statement Form within 14 days after the last appellee’s brief. Not filing signifies you don’t seek argument. Only one lawyer argues per party, and the court postpones argument only for extraordinary circumstances, not for another tribunal’s calendar. (LR 34.1(a))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Every motion starts with Form T-1080
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Every motion starts with Form T-1080. The first page of a motion is the court’s Motion Information Statement, Form T-1080. Attach supporting affidavits, and a memorandum within FRAP 27(d)(2)’s limits. Say whether you notified opposing counsel, their position, and whether they’ll respond. (LR 27.1(a))

docs.t: 2d Cir. — Emergency motions: label, notice, harm, and date
docs.x: 2d Cir.. Emergency motions: label, notice, harm, and date. A motion seeking emergency or expedited relief must be preceded by as much advance notice as possible to the clerk and opposing counsel, be labeled “Emergency Motion,” state the nature of the emergency and the harm you will suffer if it isn’t granted, and state the date by which the court must act. (2d Cir. L.R. 27.1(d); FRAP 8, 27)

You must be in good standing in a state or D.C. bar and be (1) a district-court-bar member in the circuit who tried a criminal defendant’s case and appears on the CJA appeal, (2) acting for an in forma pauperis party, or (3) able to show exceptional circumstances. docs.t: 3d Cir. — E-filing cutoff: 5:00 p.m. Eastern
docs.x: 3d Cir.. E-filing cutoff: 5:00 p.m. Eastern. A filing on the due date must be made by 5:00 p.m. Eastern time, not midnight (L.A.R. 26.1). The rule doesn’t apply to documents that initiate a proceeding, to non-ECF filers permitted to file on paper, to paper copies of briefs already filed electronically, or to inmate filings. (3d Cir. L.A.R. Misc. 113)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500. This page shows the FRAP baseline. We haven’t yet checked this circuit’s local rules for a different limit. (FRAP 32(a)(7)(B))

docs.x: 3d Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Civil briefing follows FRAP; criminal is set by order
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Civil briefing follows FRAP; criminal is set by order. In civil and agency cases the times are FRAP 31(a): 40 days for the appellant, 30 for the appellee, 21 for the reply. In direct criminal appeals the deadlines come from the clerk’s Briefing and Scheduling Order. (FRAP 31(a); court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Filing is timely until 5:00 p.m. Eastern, with exceptions
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Filing is timely until 5:00 p.m. Eastern, with exceptions. Unless a statute, local rule, or court order sets another time, documents the clerk receives by 5:00 p.m. Eastern on the last day are timely, and an electronic filing must be completed by 5:00 p.m. The rule applies to documents filed after a proceeding starts, not to documents that initiate an appeal or other proceeding. It also doesn’t apply to briefs and appendices from a party who isn’t a registered ECF filer and is allowed to file on paper, to paper copies of briefs and appendices already filed electronically, or to inmate filings under FRAP 25(a)(2)(A)(iii). Registered ECF filers must file briefs and appendices electronically and the 5:00 p.m. deadline applies. (L.A.R. 26.1 (eff. July 1, 2023); Misc. 113.3(c))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — One combined certification page
docs.x: 3d Cir.. One combined certification page. Briefs carry combined certifications covering bar membership, word count, service, identical compliance of the paper and electronic briefs, and a virus check. (Court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Every lawyer on the brief needs an appearance
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Every lawyer on the brief needs an appearance. An attorney from each office listed on the signature block must file an Entry of Appearance. (Court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Attach Volume I of the appendix to your brief
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Attach Volume I of the appendix to your brief. The court prefers that the appellant attach Volume I of the appendix to the brief. It should contain only the notice of appeal or petition for review, the order appealed, the opinion under review, and any certificate of appealability order. Statutes, rules, regulations, and unpublished opinions go in if they aren’t readily available. (Court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Covers are color-coded, with tan for supplemental briefs
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Covers are color-coded, with tan for supplemental briefs. Appellant or petitioner blue, appellee or respondent red, the third brief in a cross-appeal yellow, the appellant’s reply gray, amicus or intervenor green, and supplemental briefs tan. (Court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — A related-cases statement is required
docs.x: 3d Cir.. A related-cases statement is required. The brief needs statements of jurisdiction, issues, related cases and proceedings, and the case, with the standard or scope of review preceding each issue. The appellee’s versions are optional unless it disagrees with the appellant’s. (Court’s brief chart)

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Say where each issue was preserved
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Say where each issue was preserved. In the statement of issues, the appellant designates by specific appendix pages or place in the proceedings where each issue was raised, objected to, and ruled upon. After the issues comes a statement of related cases and proceedings, saying whether the case has been before the court before and whether you know of any related case pending or about to be presented in any court or agency. (L.A.R. 28.1(a)(1) (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Cite binding contrary authority
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Cite binding contrary authority. For each legal proposition supported by citations, counsel must cite any opposing authority that is binding on the court, such as Supreme Court decisions, published decisions of the court, and in diversity cases decisions of the highest state court. Every assertion of fact needs a specific record reference, and appendix cites are followed by a parenthetical describing the document. (L.A.R. 28.3(b) (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Footnotes are the same size as the text
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Footnotes are the same size as the text. Excessive footnotes are discouraged, and footnotes must be in the same size type as the text. Margins are at least one inch on the sides and three-quarters of an inch top and bottom, and paper documents must be firmly bound at the left with covered fasteners (L.A.R. 32.1). (L.A.R. 32.2(a) (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Extension requests have a notice rule
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Extension requests have a notice rule. A first request must show good cause, and generalities like “too busy” aren’t enough. A first request for 14 days or less may be made by phone or in writing and should be made at least 3 days before the due date. A later request must be in writing and shows good cause that wasn’t foreseeable earlier, and only one extension of a reply brief is granted. (L.A.R. 31.4 (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Joint notice of appeal means one brief and one appendix
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Joint notice of appeal means one brief and one appendix. Parties who file a joint notice of appeal get one docketed appeal, pay one fee, and must file a single consolidated brief and appendix. (L.A.R. 3.2 (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Government appellees must file a brief
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Government appellees must file a brief. A local, state, or federal entity or agency that was served below and is the appellee must file a brief whenever a schedule issues, unless the court excuses it. (L.A.R. 31.2 (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Uncontested motions must be certified
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Uncontested motions must be certified. Counsel certify that a motion is uncontested, and an uncontested motion isn’t automatically granted. Motions are decided without argument unless the court orders it (27.1). (L.A.R. 27.3 (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Summary action motions go in early
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Summary action motions go in early. Except for a change in law or circumstances, a motion for summary action or dismissal should be filed before the appellant’s brief is due, and it doesn’t stay the regular briefing schedule. (L.A.R. 27.4 (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Appendix contents and sentencing materials
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Appendix contents and sentencing materials. Volume I holds only the notice of appeal, the order or judgment appealed and related orders, the opinions or report below, and any certificate of appealability. It may be bound in the brief without counting toward length. Sealed material is filed as a separate sealed volume. In a sentencing appeal file four copies of the presentence report and statement of reasons in sealed envelopes. A deferred appendix is not favored. (L.A.R. 30.3, 32.2(c) (2011 ed.))

docs.t: 3d Cir. — Emergency motions go to the clerk, not a judge
docs.x: 3d Cir.. Emergency motions go to the clerk, not a judge. Emergency motions or applications, even if addressed to one judge, must ordinarily be filed with the clerk. If there’s no time to file, you may contact the clerk or a single judge, then file in writing as promptly as possible. The motion must briefly describe any prior actions of this court or judge on the same or a related request. (3d Cir. L.A.R. Misc. (emergency motions; former Court Rule 29.3); FRAP 8, 27)

Joining the bar,L.A.R. 46.1, 46.2 (2011 ed.),Practice is limited to bar members, and the applicant must be familiar with the federal rules and the court’s rules, especially on briefs, motions, and appendices. Apply when you enter an appearance or file a paper, though a lawyer who will argue may apply on or before argument day and must be admitted in open court on oral motion. A member or a circuit or district judge may move your admission. The initial brief must certify that an attorney on it is a member or has applied. Appellant’s counsel must file an entry of appearance within 14 days of docketing notice, others within 14 days of docketing, with an email address. The rule has no separate pro hac vice procedure. Motions: 5,200 words,FRAP 27(d)(2),A motion or response runs 5,200 words or 20 pages. A reply runs 2,600 words or 10 pages. Motion clock: 10 days, then 7,FRAP 27(a)(3),

docs.x: 4th Cir.. Briefing dates come from the clerk’s briefing order. The clerk sends a formal briefing schedule when the record is received or complete, whichever comes first, and that order controls instead of FRAP 31(a)(1). In criminal appeals the times are shortened: 35 days after the briefing order for the appellant’s brief and appendix, 21 days for the appellee’s brief, and 10 days for the reply. (LR 31(a), (b))

docs.t: 4th Cir. — Extensions are granted only for extraordinary circumstances
docs.x: 4th Cir.. Extensions are granted only for extraordinary circumstances. Move well in advance of the due date, say how much time you need and why. The court discourages these motions and may deny them or grant less time than you ask for. (LR 31(c))

docs.t: 4th Cir. — File the docketing statement within 14 days
docs.x: 4th Cir.. File the docketing statement within 14 days. Counsel who file a notice of appeal or petition must complete the court’s docketing statement and file it within 14 days of docketing, with any transcript order attached. Missing it starts the dismissal process under LR 45. Tell the clerk in writing within 10 days if the other side’s statement is inaccurate. (LR 3(b))

docs.x: 4th Cir.. Disclosure statement within 14 days of docketing. Most parties must file the court’s disclosure form within 14 days of docketing, even if they have nothing to disclose. LR 26.1 asks for more than FRAP 26.1, including publicly held companies with a direct financial interest through insurance, indemnity, or similar agreements. (LR 26.1(d))

docs.t: 4th Cir. — Ask to exceed the length limit at least 10 days early

docs.t: 4th Cir. — Sealed material needs a certificate and two versions

Sealed material in a brief or motion requires a full sealed version and a redacted public version, filed with the SEALED entries in CM/ECF and served on paper. (LR 25(c))

docs.t: 4th Cir. — Cite the appendix for every fact
docs.x: 4th Cir.. Cite the appendix for every fact. The statement of the case must tell all the facts you need, with a reference to the appendix page for each one, and appendix citations must follow the court’s Appendix Pagination and Brief Citation Guide. Appendix pages are numbered with the PDF software’s Bates numbering. (LR 28(f), 28(g))

docs.t: 4th Cir. — Emergency stay and injunction motions: panels, not single judges
docs.x: 4th Cir.. Emergency stay and injunction motions: panels, not single judges. Present all motions, including emergency motions, to the clerk for the Court; go to a single judge only in exceptional circumstances when a panel can’t act in time, and then notify the clerk’s office and give the clerk copies as soon as practical. An order granting a stay or injunction pending appeal lasts until the mandate issues or the Court orders otherwise, and may be conditioned on a supersedeas bond in the district court. (4th Cir. Local Rules 8, 27(e); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.x: 5th Cir.. Readmission every five years, $50. The clerk notifies you when renewal is due. Pay the $50 renewal fee (FJC 2024 confirms the amount) within 30 days, online. docs.t: 5th Cir. — The appellant’s brief is due 40 days after the briefing notice
docs.x: 5th Cir.. The appellant’s brief is due 40 days after the briefing notice. The appellant must send the brief to the clerk no later than 40 days after the date of the briefing notice. When the appellant serves by mail or carrier, the appellee has 33 days from the appellant’s certificate of service. That 33 days can’t be combined with the extra three days under FRAP 26(c). (5th Cir. R. 31.3)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Filing is timely until 11:59 p.m. Central
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Filing is timely until 11:59 p.m. Central. A filing must be completed by 11:59 p.m. Central Time to be timely that day. Except for briefs and record excerpts, a paper is untimely unless the clerk actually receives it within the filing period (R. 26.1). (5th Cir. R. 25.2.4)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Every brief starts with a certificate of interested persons
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Every brief starts with a certificate of interested persons. The court uses a certificate of interested persons in place of a separate disclosure statement. It goes on the first page of each brief, before the table of contents. It must list everyone with a financial interest in the outcome, including insurers, guarantors, and affiliates, and the names of opposing counsel and firms. Update it whenever the information changes. (5th Cir. R. 28.2.1)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Record excerpts replace the appendix
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Record excerpts replace the appendix. The court decides appeals on the original record, so you file record excerpts, not a FRAP 30 appendix. Mandatory contents include the docket sheet, notice of appeal, the judgment or order appealed, the verdict, and any magistrate judge’s report. The optional contents are limited to 40 pages, and the cover is durable white and marked RECORD EXCERPTS. (5th Cir. R. 30.1)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Every record assertion needs a page cite
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Every record assertion needs a page cite. Support every statement about the record with a reference to the page of the original record, in the record citation form the clerk directs. (5th Cir. R. 28.2.2)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — The oral argument statement goes at the front
docs.x: 5th Cir.. The oral argument statement goes at the front. The appellant’s principal brief must open with a short statement of why argument would help, or a waiver of argument. The appellee must also say whether argument is needed. Waiving argument is not looked on with favor once the case is calendared. (5th Cir. R. 28.2.3)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Extension requests: 7 days ahead, 30 days criminal and 40 civil at most
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Extension requests: 7 days ahead, 30 days criminal and 40 civil at most. The clerk must receive the request at least 7 days before the due date. Generalities like “too busy” don’t count. Extensions are not automatic, and absent the most compelling reasons are capped at 30 days in criminal cases and 40 days in civil cases. A pending motion doesn’t toll the deadline, and extensions for reply briefs are greatly disfavored. (5th Cir. R. 31.4; I.O.P. to R. 27)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Emergency motions have a strict form
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Emergency motions have a strict form. Call the clerk’s office and opposing counsel first. Label the motion “Emergency Motion,” state the irreparable harm, certify the facts, give the date by which you need action, attach the district court’s order and filings, serve opposing counsel at the same time, and file it by 2:00 p.m. that day. For a non-emergency that still needs action by a date certain, phone the clerk by 2:00 p.m. on the day you file. (5th Cir. R. 27.3)

docs.t: 5th Cir. — Emergency motions go to the clerk; call if no time to file
docs.x: 5th Cir.. Emergency motions go to the clerk; call if no time to file. Emergency motions or applications must be filed with the clerk, not an individual judge. If there isn’t time to file, call the clerk and then file in writing as soon as possible. The motion must briefly describe the prior actions of this or any other court or judge on the same or a related request, and stay motions must attach the documents 5th Cir. R. 8.1 requires. (5th Cir. R. 8.4, 27.3; FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Briefs: 13,000 words; replies 6,500. The Sixth Circuit follows FRAP’s 13,000-word limit. (FRAP 32(a)(7)(B))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 6th Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. That includes footnotes. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Cite the record with a description, an RE number, and Page ID
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Cite the record with a description, an RE number, and Page ID. Every citation to the district court record gives a short description of the document, the record entry number (RE or R.; avoid D, DE, or Doc.), and the Page ID range, for example “Motion for Summary Judgment, RE 23, Page ID # 120-145.” The Page ID appears in blue in the PDF header or footer from the district court docket. For a sealed document you can’t see the Page ID of, explain in a footnote and cite the entry and page, such as sealed entry 23, page 3. In agency review, cite the administrative record page, with no Page ID. (6 Cir. R. 28(a)(1))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Don’t check “argument requested” without a reasons statement
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Don’t check “argument requested” without a reasons statement. A party who wants oral argument must put a statement in the brief explaining why the court should hear it. If the CM/ECF entry says argument was requested and the statement is missing, you’ll be directed to file a corrected brief. The court says no eligible party is excluded from argument for not asking. (6 Cir. R. 34(a))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Every principal brief carries a designation of documents as an addendum
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Every principal brief carries a designation of documents as an addendum. Each party includes at the end of its principal brief an addendum designating the complaint or indictment, relevant pleadings and motions, the judgment appealed, relevant opinions, findings, and magistrate judge reports with the objections, the notice of appeal, and other necessary record parts including transcript pages. Each entry gives the record entry number, a description, and the Page ID range. Make sure every document is in the electronic district court record with a Page ID, or the brief may be rejected. (6 Cir. R. 28(b)(1), 30(g)(1))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — An appendix is required only in a few case types, and otherwise barred
docs.x: 6th Cir.. An appendix is required only in a few case types, and otherwise barred. An appendix is required only for a district court appeal where R. 30(b)(2) calls for documents not in the district court’s electronic record (such as unpublished state opinions and the trial transcript in § 2254 appeals), for Tax Court appeals, and for agency petitions, except Social Security and immigration cases, where the administrative record is filed instead. In other cases an appendix is unnecessary and must not be filed. When required it holds the current docket sheet, the listed items not in the electronic record, a certification that the documents are properly part of the record, and the other necessary parts in chronological order. You may not put documents from the district court’s electronic record in an appendix. (6 Cir. R. 30(a), (b))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Colored covers aren’t required for electronic briefs
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Colored covers aren’t required for electronic briefs. Include the case number, court name, case title, nature of the proceeding, party designation, and counsel’s name, address, and phone, but color is not required for electronically filed briefs. (Court’s brief checklist)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Footnotes are the same size as the text
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Footnotes are the same size as the text. Use a 14-point proportionally spaced font, or a monospaced font of no more than 10½ characters per inch, and keep footnotes the same size as the text. Headings, footnotes, and quotations count toward the word limit, and 6 Cir. R. 32(b) lists what is excluded. (Court’s brief checklist)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Tell the court early when you can’t argue
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Tell the court early when you can’t argue. Cases are set for argument early. Give the clerk your unavailable dates for the next nine months, preferably by the time the appellee’s brief is filed, using the Counsel Unavailability Form, and update it as conflicts arise. (Clerk’s briefing letter)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — One brief per notice of appeal, one reply
docs.x: 6th Cir.. One brief per notice of appeal, one reply. Appellants who file one notice of appeal file a single brief unless the court allows separate ones, and an appellant files one reply regardless of how many appellee briefs there are. In cross-appeals, file every brief in every case unless you are a party to only one. (FRAP 3(b)(1); checklist)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Electronic filing is mandatory and paper is refused
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Electronic filing is mandatory and paper is refused. All documents are filed through ECF in native PDF where possible, the clerk won’t accept a paper filing when electronic filing is required, and the clerk won’t accept a paper brief from a party required to file one electronically. Electronic filing in the court of appeals ends the day at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s office, which is in Cincinnati. (6 Cir. R. 25(a), 31(a))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Extensions: written motion, and unopposed isn’t enough
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Extensions: written motion, and unopposed isn’t enough. Seek an extension only by written motion. That the other side doesn’t oppose, or that you had a prior extension, isn’t dispositive, and the court disfavors extensions for briefs. In a criminal appeal say whether the defendant is in custody or on bail. A document filed late needs its own motion explaining why. (6 Cir. R. 26(a))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — The briefing clock is the clerk’s
docs.x: 6th Cir.. The briefing clock is the clerk’s. The court sets the briefing schedule, and the appellant’s date is as the clerk indicates because the electronic record is no longer “filed.” Other dates follow FRAP 31(a). Expedited briefing applies to preliminary injunction appeals, recalcitrant witness appeals, direct criminal appeals with a sentence of 15 months or less, and grand jury contempt appeals. In capital cases the appellee has 60 days and the reply is due in 14. (6 Cir. R. 31(c))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Disclosure: with your first brief, motion, or response
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Disclosure: with your first brief, motion, or response. All parties and amici in civil, bankruptcy, agency, and original proceedings, and corporate defendants in criminal cases, except government parties, file the court’s form. A negative report is required except for individual criminal defendants. It covers parents and affiliates of publicly owned companies and publicly owned companies with a substantial financial interest by insurance, franchise, or indemnity. File it with the brief or when you file a motion, response, petition, or answer, whichever is first. (6 Cir. R. 26.1)

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Motions: only jurisdictional or threshold dismissals, and no motions to affirm
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Motions: only jurisdictional or threshold dismissals, and no motions to affirm. A party may move to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction or threshold procedural grounds, and the court ordinarily won’t grant other motions to dismiss. It won’t consider a motion to affirm. All motions, emergency ones included, go to the clerk, and an emergency motion must attach the notice of appeal, the order appealed, and necessary record parts. (6 Cir. R. 27(d), (e))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — The oral argument statement is one page, and silence waives argument
docs.x: 6th Cir.. The oral argument statement is one page, and silence waives argument. A party who wants argument must include a statement of no more than one page explaining why, placed before the jurisdictional statement and excluded from the length limit. The court may deem argument waived if a party doesn’t request it in the brief or if the parties stipulate. (6 Cir. R. 34(a), (b); 28(b)(1)(B))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — The certificate of compliance goes right after the signature
docs.x: 6th Cir.. The certificate of compliance goes right after the signature. It must immediately follow the signature at the end of the brief. The disclosure statement, the designation of documents, the oral argument statement, and copies of unpublished opinions don’t count toward the length limits. (6 Cir. R. 32(a), (b))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Postponement needs good cause and a unavailability form
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Postponement needs good cause and a unavailability form. A motion to postpone must be made immediately after notice of the hearing date, give notice to counsel and the other side’s position, and say whether you filed a Counsel Unavailability Form listing that date. (6 Cir. R. 34(d))

docs.t: 6th Cir. — Emergency motions: notify the clerk early; attach the order
docs.x: 6th Cir.. Emergency motions: notify the clerk early; attach the order. File every motion, including emergency motions, with the clerk; if time doesn’t allow, phone the clerk’s office for guidance. If you know an emergency motion may be needed, make every reasonable effort to tell the clerk early what it will seek. Attach the notice of appeal, the order appealed from, and any other parts of the record needed to decide it. (6 Cir. R. 27(a), (c); FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000; amicus 7,000
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000; amicus 7,000. A principal brief may run 14,000 words and a reply 7,000, instead of FRAP’s 13,000 and 6,500, and an amicus brief may run up to 7,000 words instead of half the principal-brief limit. (Cir. R. 32(c), 29)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Rule 28(j) letters: 350 words
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Rule 28(j) letters: 350 words. The body of a citation-of-supplemental-authority letter may not exceed 350 words. (7th Cir. practice)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — 12-point type is acceptable
docs.x: 7th Cir.. 12-point type is acceptable. A brief need not meet FRAP’s 14-point requirement. Proportionally spaced type is acceptable at 12 points or larger in the body and 11 points or larger in footnotes. A brief also needn’t lie flat when open, as long as the binding is secure and doesn’t obscure the text (R. 32(a)). (Cir. R. 32(b))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Briefing runs from docketing, not from the record
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Briefing runs from docketing, not from the record. Except in agency cases the time for briefs runs from the date the appeal is docketed, regardless of whether the record is complete, unless the court orders otherwise. That means 40 days for the appellant’s brief, 30 for the appellee, and 21 for the reply under FRAP 31(a). (Cir. R. 31(a))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — File the docketing statement within 7 days, or pay a fine
docs.x: 7th Cir.. File the docketing statement within 7 days, or pay a fine. File it with the district clerk when you file the notice of appeal, or with the court of appeals within 7 days. It must meet R. 28(a), identify prior or related appeals, describe related district court litigation, name the current occupant if a party sues in an official capacity, and in a collateral attack on a conviction give the prisoner’s place of confinement and warden. If you haven’t filed within 14 days of the notice of appeal, counsel is fined $100, and at 28 days the appeal is treated as abandoned and dismissed. If the statement is incomplete, the appellee must supply a complete one within 14 days of the appellant’s. (Cir. R. 3(c))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — The jurisdictional statement has required details
docs.x: 7th Cir.. The jurisdictional statement has required details. For federal question jurisdiction identify the provision. For diversity give the amount and each party’s citizenship: a corporation’s state of incorporation and principal place of business, and the citizenship of all members of an unincorporated association or partnership. Give the judgment date, any tolling motion and its disposition, the notice of appeal date, and for a non-final order explain why it is appealable. The appellee must state explicitly whether the appellant’s summary is complete and correct, and if not provide a complete one. (Cir. R. 28(a), (b))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Lead counsel must apply for admission by the later of 30 days from docketing or 15 days from retention
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Lead counsel must apply for admission by the later of 30 days from docketing or 15 days from retention. The lead attorney for each counseled party applies for admission by the later of 30 days from docketing or 15 days from being retained or appointed. A lawyer who will present oral argument must apply before the appellee’s brief is filed. Federal government attorneys may appear without admission. There is a local fee plus the national fee, and admission can be in chambers or in open court. (Cir. R. 46(a))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — The disclosure statement is due in 21 days and names law firms
docs.x: 7th Cir.. The disclosure statement is due in 21 days and names law firms. Each attorney for a non-governmental party or amicus, and each private attorney for a governmental party, files a separate statement listing all law firms that appeared for the party in the case, including below, or are expected to appear here, and the true name of any pseudonymous litigant (kept under seal). It is due no later than 21 days after docketing, with the first motion or response, or when the court directs, whichever is earliest, and also goes with a petition for permission to appeal, a successive collateral petition, each brief, and a rehearing en banc petition. Update within 14 days of any change. It counts as your appearance. (Cir. R. 26.1)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — One counsel of record per party
docs.x: 7th Cir.. One counsel of record per party. The attorney whose name appears on the first document filed is entered as counsel of record unless otherwise identified. Counsel of record can’t withdraw without the court’s consent unless another attorney substitutes at the same time. (Cir. R. 3(d))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Make sure the district docket is complete within 21 days
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Make sure the district docket is complete within 21 days. Within 21 days of the appeal’s filing, counsel must ensure that every electronic and non-electronic document needed for appellate review is on the district court docket. Retained counsel in a criminal case must order and pay for the transcript within 14 days of the notice of appeal (R. 10(d)). (Cir. R. 10(a)(3))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — A short appendix bound with the opening brief
docs.x: 7th Cir.. A short appendix bound with the opening brief. The appellant’s brief carries an appendix with the judgment or order under review and the opinion, findings, or oral statement of reasons. It must also include other opinions, orders, and oral rulings addressing the issues (with the transcript portion for a challenged oral ruling), magistrate, bankruptcy, and agency decisions, earlier opinions in a collateral attack, post-trial orders, and short record excerpts. These may be bound with the brief if the total is 50 pages or fewer. The appendix must state that all required materials are included. A supplemental appendix may go with the appellee’s brief, and costs for a lengthy appendix won’t be awarded. (Cir. R. 30)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Extension motions need an affidavit with specifics
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Extension motions need an affidavit with specifics. Extensions of time for briefs are not favored. The motion must state the due date and be supported by an affidavit showing that, with due diligence and giving the brief priority, filing on time is impossible, with the date and ruling on any earlier motion. Generalities such as that counsel is too busy aren’t sufficient. (Cir. R. 26)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — If a brief isn’t filed, you get an order to show cause
docs.x: 7th Cir.. If a brief isn’t filed, you get an order to show cause. A missed appellant’s brief draws an order to show cause why the appeal shouldn’t be dismissed, or in criminal and appointed-counsel civil cases within 14 days why discipline shouldn’t follow. A missed appellee’s brief draws an order to show cause within 14 days why the case shouldn’t be treated as ready and the appellee denied oral argument. (Cir. R. 31(c), (d))

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Electronic filing, with paper only by exception
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Electronic filing, with paper only by exception. All documents are filed and served electronically, except those of unrepresented non-lawyers. To be exempt, move at least seven days before the document is due, with a good reason. Electronic filing in the court of appeals ends the day at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s office, in Chicago. (Cir. R. 25)

docs.t: 7th Cir. — Emergency filings: warn the clerk during business hours
docs.x: 7th Cir.. Emergency filings: warn the clerk during business hours. If you anticipate needing emergency action while the Clerk’s Office is closed, alert the office during business hours and as early as possible. Emergency papers must still comply with Circuit Rule 25, and filings made electronically aren’t read outside business hours unless you arranged it in advance. (7th Cir. R. 27; FRAP 8, 27)

docs.x: 7th Cir.. Filing deadline: midnight Central (Chicago). For electronic filing in the court of appeals the day ends at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s office, in Chicago. (FRAP 26(a)(4)(B); Cir. R. 25)

docs.x: 8th Cir.. The opening brief is due 40 days after the docket entries are filed. docs.t: 8th Cir. — Start the brief with a one-page Summary of the Case
docs.x: 8th Cir.. Start the brief with a one-page Summary of the Case. Each appellant’s brief opens with a statement of no more than one page giving a summary of the case, the reasons why oral argument should or shouldn’t be heard, and the time needed (typically 10, 15, 20, or 30 minutes). It is the first item in the brief. The appellee may respond if it finds the appellant’s statement incorrect or incomplete. (8th Cir. R. 28A(i)(1))

docs.t: 8th Cir. — List at most four apposite cases under each issue

docs.t: 8th Cir. — File the addendum with the opening brief, as a separate document
docs.x: 8th Cir.. File the addendum with the opening brief, as a separate document. The appellant’s addendum contains the opinion or order below with its supporting memoranda, any magistrate judge’s report and recommendation, and other relevant rulings, plus up to 15 pages of record excerpts. Immigration, Social Security, and criminal appeals have their own required contents, and a criminal addendum must not include the Statement of Reasons or Presentence Report. The appellee’s optional addendum is limited to 15 pages and can’t duplicate the appellant’s. File the addendum as its own CM/ECF event, not attached to the brief. (8th Cir. R. 28A(g))

docs.t: 8th Cir. — Ten paper copies within 5 days of the filing notice

Then, within 5 days, send 10 paper copies to the clerk in St. Louis and serve one copy on each separately represented or pro se party. Failure draws an order to show cause. Cases heard en banc take 11 additional copies. (8th Cir. R. 28A(d))

docs.t: 8th Cir. — A defective brief gets five days to fix
docs.x: 8th Cir.. A defective brief gets five days to fix. If the brief doesn’t comply, the clerk gives you 5 days to submit a compliant one. docs.t: 9th Cir. — Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Briefs: 14,000 words; replies 7,000. Opening and answering briefs may each run 14,000 words, and a reply half of that. Cross-appeal briefs: 14,000 for the appellant’s principal and its response and reply, 16,500 for the appellee’s principal and response, and half of 14,000 for the appellee’s reply. Separately represented parties filing a joint brief automatically get 5 more pages or 1,400 words, and so does a party answering or replying to multiple briefs. FRAP 32(f) material is excluded, and every brief counted by words needs Form 8. (9th Cir. R. 32-1, 32-2(b), 28.1-1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 9th Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. That includes footnotes. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Cite the excerpts of record, not the district court record
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Cite the excerpts of record, not the district court record. The appellant files Excerpts of Record with the opening brief, the appellee Supplemental Excerpts only for documents not already included (or if the appellant was exempt), and the appellant Further Excerpts with the reply only for new documents. Unless you are exempt, direct citations to the district court record aren’t permitted except for undisputed background. Excerpts are filed electronically, separate from the brief. Serve one paper copy the same day on any unregistered party, and file paper copies with the court only when the clerk directs. No excerpts are needed in immigration removal petitions or by a party without counsel. (9th Cir. R. 30-1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Deadlines come from the Time Schedule Order
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Deadlines come from the Time Schedule Order. The clerk issues a Time Schedule Order with deadlines for designating the transcript, for the reporter to file it, and for the briefs. The opposition brief is due 30 days after the opening brief, and the optional reply 21 days after the opposition. (9th Cir. R. 31-2; Time Schedule Order)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — A streamlined extension: one, up to 30 days, with limits
docs.x: 9th Cir.. A streamlined extension: one, up to 30 days, with limits. You may get one streamlined extension of up to 30 days per opening, answering, reply, or cross-appeal brief if you haven’t previously moved to extend that brief. It isn’t available if the case was previously expedited, a Notice of Oral Argument has issued, or the brief is in a preliminary injunction appeal, a recalcitrant witness appeal, or a Class Action Fairness Act appeal. Request it online, or by Form 13 in the mail, on or before the due date. Any other extension needs a written motion at least 7 days before the deadline, showing diligence and substantial need, with a declaration covering the seven points in R. 31-2.2(b). (9th Cir. R. 31-2.2)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Motions to exceed length: on or before the due date
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Motions to exceed length: on or before the due date. The court disfavors them and grants them only on diligence and extraordinary and compelling need, such as a multi-defendant criminal case with a lengthy trial. File on or before the brief’s due date with a declaration, a single copy of the proposed brief, and Form 8. The cost of revising the brief isn’t considered. (9th Cir. R. 32-2(a))

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Brief contents beyond FRAP 28
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Brief contents beyond FRAP 28. A jurisdiction statement before the statement of the case must state, in order, the district court or agency’s statutory basis, why the order is final or appealable and this court’s statutory basis, and the dates of judgment and notice of appeal and why the appeal is timely. A criminal opening brief states bail status and projected release date. For each issue state where it was raised and ruled on and the standard of review, plus where objections were made. A statement of related cases goes on the last page, as a certificate excluded from the length limit. Don’t incorporate or attach briefs from below or a prior appeal (R. 28-1(b)). (9th Cir. R. 28-2, 28-1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Describe any images in the text
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Describe any images in the text. When a brief includes an image, paraphrase the image’s text in the sentences before or after it, and cite the excerpts of record. Don’t let an image carry content the text doesn’t. (9th Cir. R. 32-1(f) (eff. Dec. 1, 2022))

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Electronic filing is timely until 11:59 p.m. Pacific
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Electronic filing is timely until 11:59 p.m. Pacific. Attorneys must file everything electronically unless exempted. A filing successfully completed by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time is entered as of that date. No paper copies are submitted unless the court directs, and then generally only briefs and excerpts that have been accepted. (9th Cir. R. 25-5)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — The disclosure statement is Form 34, filed separately
docs.x: 9th Cir.. The disclosure statement is Form 34, filed separately. In cases opened on or after December 1, 2024 involving non-governmental entities, bankruptcy, organizational victims, or review of state court proceedings, each party, amicus, and intervenor files Form 34 within 14 days of docketing (or with a motion filed sooner), using the “Disclosure Statement (CR 26.1-1)” filing type. Name parents and any 10% publicly held owner by registered name and ticker, name any Ninth Circuit judge who took part below, and supplement while the case is pending. Don’t put it in the brief. (9th Cir. R. 26.1-1; 28-1(c))

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Preliminary injunction appeals run on a 28-day clock
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Preliminary injunction appeals run on a 28-day clock. Caption the notice “PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION APPEAL.” Within 7 days of the notice, arrange expedited transcripts. Unless the court orders otherwise, the opening brief and excerpts are due within 28 days of docketing the notice in the district court, the appellee’s brief 28 days after service, and the reply 21 days after that. A motion to expedite or for a stay may change the schedule. (9th Cir. R. 3-3)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Format the excerpts of record exactly
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Format the excerpts of record exactly. Each volume starts with a caption page, has an index, and runs no more than 300 pages, with consecutive page numbers. Parts of the record go in reverse chronological order, newest first, with sealed material in its own final volume or volumes. Cite multi-volume excerpts as 1-ER-12 (volume, ER, page) and single-volume excerpts as ER-12. Supplemental excerpts are SER and further excerpts FER. (9th Cir. R. 30-1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Court-ordered due dates aren’t extended by the mailing allowance
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Court-ordered due dates aren’t extended by the mailing allowance. Parties must observe the briefing schedule the court orders, and specific dates set by order don’t get the 3-day mail allowance. (9th Cir. R. 31-2.1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Motions: 20 pages, responses 20, replies 10
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Motions: 20 pages, responses 20, replies 10. A motion or response may not exceed 20 pages and a reply 10, excluding FRAP 27(a)(2)(B) and 32(f) material. If the movant learns a motion is unopposed, it must tell the court, and relief needed by a date certain goes in bold on the caption page. (9th Cir. R. 27-1)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — A 28(j) letter body is 350 words
docs.x: 9th Cir.. A 28(j) letter body is 350 words. The body of a FRAP 28(j) letter can’t exceed 350 words. (9th Cir. R. 28-6)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — One principal brief per side, even against several
docs.x: 9th Cir.. One principal brief per side, even against several. A party or group of jointly represented parties files a single principal or reply brief even when responding to multiple briefs. An answering party’s reply due date runs from the last-served answering brief, and the filing of the opening brief early doesn’t advance the appellee’s date (R. 31-2.1). (9th Cir. R. 28-5)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Emergency motions: relief needed within 21 days
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Emergency motions: relief needed within 21 days. If you need relief within 21 days to avoid irreparable harm: notify the court and opposing counsel and serve the motion as early as practicable; put “Emergency Motion Under Circuit Rule 27-3” and the date relief is needed on the caption page; and include a Circuit Rule 27-3 Certificate with all counsel’s contact details, the facts showing the emergency, why it couldn’t be filed earlier, when and how you gave notice, and whether you first sought the relief in the district court or agency. Contact the emergency motions unit before or when filing. (9th Cir. R. 27-3; FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 9th Cir. — Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific
docs.x: 9th Cir.. Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific. An electronic filing successfully completed by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time is entered on the docket as of that date. The court’s Appellate Electronic Filing System determines the date and time. (9th Cir. R. 25-5(d)(2))

docs.x: 10th Cir.. 14-point type preferred; 13-point accepted. The court prefers 14-point type but accepts 13-point. Count every character in citation sentences and footnotes toward the word limit. docs.t: 10th Cir. — Opening brief and appendix: 40 days from the record-complete notice
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Opening brief and appendix: 40 days from the record-complete notice. With retained counsel on every side, the appellant’s brief and electronic appendix are due within 40 days of the date the district court clerk notifies the court that the record is complete. With appointed counsel or a pro se appellant, 40 days after the record is filed. The answer brief is due 30 days after service of the opening brief, and the reply 21 days after the answer. (10th Cir. R. 31.1; FRAP 31(a))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — File an electronic appendix with the opening brief
docs.x: 10th Cir.. File an electronic appendix with the opening brief. Retained counsel, including a lawyer representing themselves, must file an electronic appendix. Each volume has a cover and an index, runs no more than 300 pages, and is in chronological order, starting with the district court docket entries. Pages are consecutively numbered, and citations to a multi-volume appendix must give both volume and page. Hard copies are ordered only if needed, and must be an exact replica. (10th Cir. R. 30.1)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Attach the rulings to the brief, even though they’re in the appendix
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Attach the rulings to the brief, even though they’re in the appendix. The appellant’s brief must attach every pertinent written finding, conclusion, opinion, or order below, with the magistrate judge’s report if the district court adopted it, transcript pages for oral rulings, the judgment, and in Social Security and immigration cases the agency decisions. If the appellant doesn’t attach them all, the appellee’s brief must. Attachments are listed in the table of contents. (10th Cir. R. 28.2(A), (B))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Cover, argument statement, related appeals, glossary
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Cover, argument statement, related appeals, glossary. The cover names the court, the judge whose judgment is appealed, and the originating case number. Each party’s first brief states on the cover whether argument is requested, with the reasons after the conclusion if it is. The first brief lists all prior or related appeals at the end of the table of authorities, or says there are none, and a glossary follows the table of authorities if you use uncommon acronyms. The glossary can be excluded from the word count (R. 32(B)). (10th Cir. R. 28.2(C))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Disclosure statement: Form 4, a separate filing
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Disclosure statement: Form 4, a separate filing. File Form 4 as a separate filing, not in the brief, within 14 days after docketing, or when you file a motion, response, answer, or amicus brief, whichever is first. Hard copies aren’t required. Amend it promptly if the information changes. (10th Cir. R. 26.1)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Motions to exceed word counts are disfavored
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Motions to exceed word counts are disfavored. They are denied absent extraordinary and compelling circumstances. A motion filed within 14 days of the brief’s due date must show why earlier filing wasn’t possible. (10th Cir. R. 28.3(A))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — File the transcript order form even if there is no transcript
docs.x: 10th Cir.. File the transcript order form even if there is no transcript. Within 14 days after the notice of appeal, the appellant files the court’s transcript order form, or states why no transcript is being ordered. (10th Cir. R. 10.2)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Joint briefing is the default in civil appeals
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Joint briefing is the default in civil appeals. Multiple appellants or appellees must brief jointly to the greatest extent possible. A separate brief needs a certificate of counsel explaining why, unless a government entity is the only other party on that side. (10th Cir. R. 31.3)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — In diversity cases, LLCs and partnerships must list their members’ citizenship
docs.x: 10th Cir.. In diversity cases, LLCs and partnerships must list their members’ citizenship. When jurisdiction rests on 28 U.S.C. § 1332 and a party is an LLC, partnership, or other unincorporated entity, that party’s brief must identify each member and the member’s state of citizenship, and file a supplemental statement if the information changes. (10th Cir. R. 28.2(C)(6))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Entry of appearance carries a certificate of interested parties
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Entry of appearance carries a certificate of interested parties. Within 14 days after docketing, counsel file the court’s entry of appearance (Form 2). Each one is accompanied by a certificate listing all interested persons and entities not in the notice of appeal’s caption, including parents, insurers, and affiliates, and attorneys who appeared below or in related proceedings, or stating that there are none. Keep it current. (10th Cir. R. 46.1)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Fees: pay within 14 days of docketing or risk dismissal
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Fees: pay within 14 days of docketing or risk dismissal. An appeal may be dismissed immediately if within 14 days after docketing a party fails to pay the fee, move to extend the time to pay, or move for leave to proceed without prepayment. (10th Cir. R. 3.3(B))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Motions to dismiss for jurisdiction: 14 days after docketing
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Motions to dismiss for jurisdiction: 14 days after docketing. The court allows only motions to dismiss, for summary disposition because of a change of law or mootness, to remand, and by the government to enforce an appeal waiver. The first three are due within 14 days after docketing, absent good cause, and a government appeal-waiver motion within 20 days after the record-complete notice. Responses are due in 14 days. A dispositive motion suspends briefing unless the court orders otherwise. (10th Cir. R. 27.3(A))

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Every motion states the other side’s position
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Every motion states the other side’s position. A motion must state the opposing party’s position or why you couldn’t learn it, and amici must do the same on a motion for leave. Motions in direct criminal appeals to withdraw or substitute counsel are exempt. (10th Cir. R. 27.1; 29.2)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Stay and emergency motions: required showing and certificate
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Stay and emergency motions: required showing and certificate. A stay or injunction motion must state the specific relief and address jurisdiction (district court and appellate), likelihood of success, irreparable harm, harm to opposing parties, and the public interest, or it won’t be considered. A motion asking for a ruling within five days must be marked “EMERGENCY” with a certificate stating why it wasn’t filed earlier, when the order was entered and takes effect, and all counsel’s phone numbers and emails. Notify the Clerk in advance. Applications to a single judge are disfavored. (10th Cir. R. 8.1, 8.2, 8.3; FRAP 8, 27)

docs.t: 10th Cir. — Filing deadline: midnight Mountain
docs.x: 10th Cir.. Filing deadline: midnight Mountain. For electronic filing in the court of appeals, the last day ends at midnight in the time zone of the circuit clerk’s principal office, in Denver. (FRAP 26(a)(4)(B))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Pay the $20 renewal fee every five years
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Pay the $20 renewal fee every five years. Pay the bar membership renewal fee the court posts every five years from your admission date. The clerk sends notice in the first week of the due month and payment is due by that month’s last day. If the notice bounces because your contact information is stale, no further notice is sent. Unpaid, you go inactive and may not practice before the court. After 12 months inactive the clerk strikes your name from the roll. The court’s website lists the fee as $20. (11th Cir. R. 46-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — 14-point type
docs.x: 11th Cir.. 14-point type. FRAP 32(a)(5) requires a proportionally spaced serif face of 14 points or larger. (FRAP 32(a)(5))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Certify compliance
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Briefing times follow FRAP 31
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Briefing times follow FRAP 31. The appellant’s brief is due 40 days after the record is filed, the appellee’s 30 days after service of the appellant’s brief, and the reply 21 days after the appellee’s. The clerk sends a letter confirming the date, but a missed letter doesn’t change the deadline. (11th Cir. R. 31-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The CIP: 14 days for appellants, 28 for appellees, or at your first filing
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The CIP: 14 days for appellants, 28 for appellees, or at your first filing. Appellants and petitioners file the Certificate of Interested Persons and Corporate Disclosure Statement within 14 days after docketing, or with their first filing if earlier. Appellees, intervenors, and respondents file within 28 days, or with their first filing if earlier, whether or not the appellant has filed, and may instead file a notice that an existing CIP is correct and complete or adds omitted persons. A petition that starts a proceeding carries its CIP. Every amicus puts a CIP in every motion and brief. On the same day you first file a CIP, counsel must complete the court’s web-based CIP, entering stock ticker symbols or “nothing to declare.” (11th Cir. R. 26.1-1)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Fix a deficient brief within 14 days or lose the appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Fix a deficient brief within 14 days or lose the appeal. In a civil appeal, failing to correct a deficiency in a brief or appendix within 14 days of the clerk’s notice leads to dismissal. A request for more time to correct must also come within that 14 days. (11th Cir. R. 42-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Missing the appellant’s brief deadline can end the appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Missing the appellant’s brief deadline can end the appeal. In a civil appeal, the appeal is dismissed if the appellant doesn’t file the brief or the appendix by the due date. (11th Cir. R. 42-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Paper copies only when the clerk asks
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Paper copies only when the clerk asks. At the end of briefing the clerk sends each party a notice directing it to send the court two paper copies of its brief or briefs. Pro se parties aren’t required to. (11th Cir. R. 31-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — No appearance form, no processing
docs.x: 11th Cir.. No appearance form, no processing. The clerk generally can’t process an attorney’s filings until the attorney files an appearance form, which is due within 14 days of the clerk’s notice. For a lawyer who isn’t a member of the bar, the clerk may conditionally file certain papers, such as a time-sensitive motion, and then gives 21 days to apply for admission or pro hac vice status. (11th Cir. R. 46-5, 46-6)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Nothing is acted on until the CIP and web-based CIP are done
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Nothing is acted on until the CIP and web-based CIP are done. The court won’t act on any papers, emergency filings included, until the CIP is filed and the web-based CIP completed, except to prevent manifest injustice. The clerk can’t submit a brief or motion to the court without them, and failure can mean dismissal under R. 42-1(b). (11th Cir. R. 26.1-5)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The table of citations: no passim, and asterisk your key cases
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The table of citations: no passim, and asterisk your key cases. List every page on which an authority is cited, using ranges if it’s cited on every page of the range, and mark with asterisks in the margin the citations you primarily rely on. (11th Cir. R. 28-1(d))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — The summary of argument: seldom two pages, never five
docs.x: 11th Cir.. The summary of argument: seldom two pages, never five. It must be a condensation of the argument actually made, not a repeat of the headings. Criminal appeals must say whether the client is incarcerated, and the statement of facts must include unfavorable facts and identify inferences as inferences. (11th Cir. R. 28-1(i))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Cite the record by document number and page, and say which format you use
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Cite the record by document number and page, and say which format you use. The transcript page is the one in the header generated by the district court’s electronic filing system if available, otherwise the court reporter’s page number. The brief must note the format. (11th Cir. R. 28-5)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Only the cover and the signature block may be single-spaced
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Only the cover and the signature block may be single-spaced. Only the cover page, certificate of service, direct quotes, headings, and footnotes may be single-spaced. Everything else is double-spaced, including the tables. A noncompliant brief can be rejected or conditionally filed, with replacement briefs due within 14 days of the clerk’s notice. (11th Cir. R. 32-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Move to exceed length at least 7 days early
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Move to exceed length at least 7 days early. A motion for leave to file an overlength brief must be filed at least 7 days before the due date and is granted only for extraordinary and compelling reasons. Front matter and statutory addenda don’t count toward the limit. (11th Cir. R. 32-4)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Appellee’s supplemental appendix: 7 days after its brief
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Appellee’s supplemental appendix: 7 days after its brief. If the appellant’s appendix is deficient or the appellee’s brief relies on record parts not in it, the appellee files a supplemental appendix within seven days of filing its brief, without duplicating the appellant’s. Only documents submitted to the trial court may go in the appendix, except state court opinions in a § 2254 appeal. (11th Cir. R. 30-1(b))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Pending motions move the brief deadline
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Pending motions move the brief deadline. If a motion to proceed in forma pauperis, for a certificate of appealability, of a type in FRAP 4(a)(4)(A) or 4(b)(3)(A), about excusable neglect, for appointment or withdrawal of counsel, or for a transcript at government expense is pending, the appellant’s brief is due 40 days after it is resolved or 40 days after the record is deemed filed, whichever is later. The appellee gets 30 days. Otherwise a pending motion doesn’t postpone a brief. (11th Cir. R. 31-1(b))

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Extension requests have four rules to know
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Extension requests have four rules to know. A first request for 30 days or less may be made by phone or in writing and the clerk can grant it. A first request for more than 30 days must be a written motion filed at least 7 days before the due date. If a first request filed 14 or more days ahead is denied within 7 days of the due date or later, you automatically get 7 more days. A second request is extremely disfavored and needs extraordinary, unforeseeable circumstances, and no request is accepted after the due date. (11th Cir. R. 31-2)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Rehearing: 21 days, and en banc is extraordinary
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Rehearing: 21 days, and en banc is extraordinary. File a petition for panel or en banc rehearing within 21 days of judgment, or 45 days in a civil appeal where the United States is a party. En banc review is for precedent-setting errors of exceptional importance or a conflict with precedent, not state-law, factual, or sufficiency errors. A rehearing petition against a stay, counsel, or leave-to-appeal order is treated as a motion to reconsider instead. (11th Cir. R. 40-2, 40-6, 40-7)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Reconsideration of a motion order: 21 days, and only once
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Reconsideration of a motion order: 21 days, and only once. Move to reconsider, vacate, or modify an order within 21 days, with no extra time for mailing. You get one motion per order, and you can’t seek reconsideration of the order that disposes of it. (11th Cir. R. 27-2, 27-3)

docs.t: 11th Cir. — Failing to object to a magistrate judge’s report waives appeal
docs.x: 11th Cir.. Failing to object to a magistrate judge’s report waives appeal. If you were told the time to object and the consequences, not objecting waives your right to challenge unobjected-to factual and legal conclusions on appeal. The court may still review for plain error when justice requires. (11th Cir. R. 3-1)

docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Certify compliance. Every brief needs a certificate stating the word count and confirming the typeface and type-style rules are met. (FRAP 32(g))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The briefing schedule is set by order
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The briefing schedule is set by order. The court issues a scheduling order and the briefs are due on its dates, not the FRAP 31(a) default clock. (D.C. Cir. R. 31(a))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Open with the Certificate as to Parties, Rulings, and Related Cases
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Open with the Certificate as to Parties, Rulings, and Related Cases. Immediately inside the cover and before the table of contents, every brief (including intervenor and amicus briefs) needs a certificate with separate paragraphs, in the same order, for parties and amici, rulings under review, and related cases. The appellant lists every party, intervenor, and amicus in the district court and here, and an appellee may adopt that list with a set sentence. Rulings need the date, the judge’s name, the place in the appendix, and the official or Federal Register citation. Related cases means substantially the same parties and the same or similar issues, in any other court of appeals or any other federal or local court in D.C., and if there are none the certificate says so. Entities include the Rule 26.1 disclosure. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(1))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Length: what is excluded
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Length: what is excluded. Length follows FRAP 28.1 and 32(a)(7). In addition to the FRAP 32(f) items, the certificate of parties, rulings, and related cases, the glossary, and any addendum of standing evidence may be excluded from the word count. An intervenor’s principal brief is limited to 19 pages and its reply to 9, unless it complies with the word limits in R. 32(e)(2). (D.C. Cir. R. 32(e)(1); 28(c))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — In direct agency review, a Standing section is required
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. In direct agency review, a Standing section is required. The brief of an appellant or petitioner in direct review of administrative action must set out the basis for standing in a section titled “Standing” that follows the summary of argument and immediately precedes the argument. It must argue and cite evidence showing standing by a “substantial probability.” Evidence not in the administrative record goes in an addendum, separated from the brief by a colored page, and bound separately if over 40 pages. A brief with a Standing section needn’t have the summary of argument rule’s placement. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(7))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Say “Complex” on the cover
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Say “Complex” on the cover. In cases the court designates “Complex,” the cover of the brief should say so. (Handbook § IX.A.6)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The table of authorities: no passim, optional asterisks
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The table of authorities: no passim, optional asterisks. The table must identify each page where an authority is cited, and passim or similar terms may not be used, in the table or in record and authority citations. You may asterisk the authorities you chiefly rely on, with the notation at the bottom of the first page of the table. A glossary on the page right after the table must define every abbreviation or acronym that isn’t common usage. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(2), (b))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Statutes and regulations: in the brief or an addendum
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Statutes and regulations: in the brief or an addendum. Pertinent statutes and regulations go in the body after the statement of issues, or in an addendum with its own table of contents, introduced by a statement in the brief. An addendum over 40 pages must be bound separately, and one bound with the brief is separated by a distinctly colored page. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(5))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Say on the cover if the case is argued or submitted
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Say on the cover if the case is argued or submitted. If a case has been scheduled for argument, already argued, or is submitted without argument, the brief must say so in capital letters at the top of the front cover, with the argument date where applicable. Motions, responses, and replies must say the same at the top of page one (R. 27(a)(3)). (D.C. Cir. R. 28(a)(8))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Extension and length motions: at least 7 days before the brief is due
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Extension and length motions: at least 7 days before the brief is due. The court disfavors motions to exceed length or extend brief time that affect the oral argument schedule and grants them only for extraordinarily compelling reasons. File at least 7 days before the due date, attempt to get the other side’s consent first, and recite the other side’s position in the opening paragraph. Untimely motions are denied absent exceptional circumstances, though the clerk may grant an unopposed late motion for an extension that doesn’t affect argument. (D.C. Cir. R. 28(e))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — The briefing schedule is the court’s scheduling order
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The briefing schedule is the court’s scheduling order. Parties serve and file briefs by the scheduling order, including in cross-appeals. File the original and 8 copies of every brief (for ECF filers, 8 paper copies follow the electronic filing within two business days by first-class mail), except that in a deferred-appendix case initial briefs go in electronic form only. (D.C. Cir. R. 31(a), 28.1(c))

docs.x: D.C. Cir.. The docketing statement and provisional certificate. As the court directs, the appellant files a docketing statement on the clerk’s form with a provisional certificate containing the information Rule 28(a)(1) requires. R. 12)

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Dispositive motions within 45 days of docketing
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Dispositive motions within 45 days of docketing. A motion that would dispose of the appeal or petition entirely, or transfer the case, must be filed within 45 days of docketing unless a scheduling order sets another time. Briefing is deferred pending a timely one. Attach the pertinent opinion or findings, or the transcript extract if the reasons were oral. (D.C. Cir. R. 27(f))

docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Every motion carries the certificate and disclosure statement. Attach as an addendum a certificate of parties and amici as in Rule 28(a)(1)(A) and any required disclosure statement, unless already filed, and file the original and 4 copies unless the court directs otherwise. A response combined with a cross-motion for affirmative relief may run 7,800 words, and the answer to it, with any reply, is due within 10 days and limited to 5,200 words. (D.C. Cir. R. 27(a)(4), (b))

docs.t: D.C. Cir. — Stays and emergency relief: the four factors, with specificity
docs.x: D.C. Cir.. Stays and emergency relief: the four factors, with specificity. Try to notify the other side by phone before filing and describe those efforts. Attach the order and any decision or findings (or the transcript extract if oral), plus the certificate of parties and amici and the disclosure statement. (D.C. Cir. R. 8(a); FRAP 8, 27)
